newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK SARANTOPOULOS' CONVERTIBLES MAKE DEBUT THURSDAY.
newsitem.headline: GREEK SARANTOPOULOS' CONVERTIBLES MAKE DEBUT THURSDAY.

text.p: Greek construction firm Sarantopoulos' convertible bonds will start trading on the Athens stock exchange on Thursday, the company said in a statement.
Delivery of the 9.0 percent, five-year convertible bonds will commense on February 5, it said.

Sarantopoulos raised 2.52 billion drachmas by selling 1,445,310 convertible bonds at 1,750 drachmas each to finance its participation in the Rio-Antirrio bridge and Elefsis-Stavros-Spata highway projects, it said.
The conversion price is 2,100 drachmas fixed for the life of the bond and the conversion ratio is 10 bonds, the minimum lot, for 10 shares.
The firm retains the right to call the convertibles after a year if its share price on the Athens bourse exceeds 3,000 drachmas.
Societe Generale Banque, Athens was the issue advisor to the company.
The orderbook of Sarantopoulos currently stands at 48 billion drachmas. The 1996 turnover of the firm was 9.3 billion drachmas and its pre-tax profits at 1.8 billion.
